- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–3% to match recent momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior high), model frequently overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction of 1–3% to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 3–5 day window and reduce forecast slope accordingly.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates the final 5–7 days; apply a “tail correction” by subtracting 1–3% from the last 5–7 forecast points.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and prices are volatile, model tends to smooth too much; allow for 1–2% volatility buffer in forecast midpoints.
